entries.english:
Property inventories I–W, arranged by owner. Entries include: Ilbenstadt Abbey (1733/1763); J. Fr. Jacobi, Amtmann at Birkenfeld and son-in-law of Aegidius Herdenius, Amtmann at Rödelheim (Ossenheim), concerning Ossenheim (1682); G. H. von Jossa and Kirberg at Bermbach in the Untertaunus district (1735); the Jungmann family at Marburg and Kassel, co-owner Hein, and Nassau-Orange district envoy B. J. von Eck, concerning Mittelburg at Bellersheim (1706/1763); von Kameytsky at Alzenau, Kälberau, and Michelbach (c. 1750); and von Kirchheim holdings at Heldenbergen, Kaichen, Kilianstädten, Nieder-Wöllstadt, “Soda,” Stammheim, Steinfurth, Harheim, Bonames, Kalbach, Wachenbuchen, Dörnigheim, Groß-Karben, Naumburg, and Nieder-Florstadt, partly acquired from von Bechtolsheim (1648/1706). Also listed are the Teutonic Order commandery at Kloppenheim and its Okarben property (1763); J. H. Koch at Altenstadt (1764); Kratz and associates at Nieder-Florstadt (1764); von Kroneck field names at Groß-Karben (1690/1763); and the Krug [von Nidda] holdings, then associated with Mrs. Humberger of Marburg and Mrs. Vigelius of Ranstadt, both née Schmitt, Mrs. Rencker, née Krug, at Geiß-Nidda, and Lieutenant Volhard, concerning about twelve hides at Wisselsheim (c. 1700).

The list further records J. J. Lantz, pastor at Auerbach, and [Councillor] Gerber of Darmstadt, concerning Rendel (1745/1764); von Lauter at Ober-Hörgen, Bönstadt, Butzbach, Gambach, Okriftel, Nauheim, Dörnigheim, and “Kestadt” (1668/1761); J. Linden of Frankfurt and the “Edelmann” vineyard (1739); Loew von Steinfurth at Nieder-Florstadt, Echzell, Heegheim, Heuchelheim, the Büdingen district, Kostheim, Berstadt, Kinzenbach, Weckesheim, Ockstadt, Rödelheim, Kirch-Göns, Staden, Mockstadt, Ostheim, Fauerbach vor der Höhe, Wickstadt, Münzenberg, Bauernheim, Okarben, Friedberg, Wisselsheim, Nieder-Bessingen, Grüningen, Holzheim, and Bruchenbrücken (1630/1763); Privy Councillor Lucius’s heirs at Gambach with M. H. Mettingh (1763); the Teutonic Order at Marburg and Steinfurth (1763/1788); von Marioth at Geisenheim and elsewhere (1726); and the Massing heirs, including Oberschultheiß Schultz and J. Philipp Kartz, at Merenberg (1712/1797). Further entries concern Merlau at Philippseck near Heddernheim, Groß-Karben, and Holzhausen (1698/1711); von Metternich (1729) and Ober-Mörlen (1748); von Meuseren at Hadamar, Weyer, and elsewhere in the Oberlahn district, Waldernbach, and Ellar, later in part held by von Eyß (1685/1771); Molitor heirs at Merenberg and notary J. Gasteyer of Weilburg (1729); von Nagel (1749/1750); and Nassau-Orange, hereditary stadtholder of the Netherlands, concerning the Schönbach estate in the Dill district, formerly held by Heppenberg and then Quadt von Landskron, with earlier files and extracts from 1542 onward (1729/1772).

Other entries concern the Graf von Neuwied’s Hachenburg properties (1749); Palatinate-Zweibrücken-Birkenfeld at Gelnhausen, formerly Grempisch (1699); Balthasar Pfeiffer at Esck, formerly von Hohenfeld (1733); von Nordeck zur Rabenau at Trais-Münzenberg, Obbornhofen, Ulfa, Bellersheim (formerly Riedesel von Bellersheim), Altenstadt, and Griedel (1651/1764); Rau zu Holzhausen at Dorheim, Beienheim, and Holzhausen vor der Höhe (1764/1765); the widow M. von Rauchenhausen at Groß- and Klein-Karben and Kloppenheim (1763); Freiherr von Reiffenberg zu Sayn at Sayn, Engers, Bendorf, Dietkirchen, Eschhofen, Balduinstein, Nieder-Selters, and elsewhere (1735); von Reineck at Ober-Eschbach, formerly held by Prince Josef zu Loewenstein or Mrs. M. V. von Hausen, née Überacker (1747/1756); another Reineck record at Ober-Eschbach, formerly von Rottenhoff (1740/1756); Rencker at Wisselsheim and Münzenberg (1714); and J. Reiprecht von Büdingen at Marköbel, Hüttengesäß, Bettenhausen, Groß-Buseck, Reiskirchen, Burkhardsfelden, Bauernheim, Assenheim, Wenings, Vonhausen, Mittel-Gründau, Diebach am Haag, Pferdsbach, Dudenrod, Orleshausen, and elsewhere (1629). Also listed are Kitz, Schultheiß, at Rendel (1765); Philipp W. von Riedt of Fritzlar, royal-imperial Generalfeldzeugmeister, concerning Heddernheim, Rockenberg, Hees, Esch, Dottenfelderhof, Geisenheim on the Rhine, Hattenheim, Eschersheim, Praunheim, and field names (1696, 1752); the Ritter family at Grünstein, concerning Hasselhecke, Eschborn, Eltville, and Rüdesheim (1735/1763); J. J. Rode at Ober-Eschbach (1697); and a c. 1760 inventory of knightly properties at Romsthal, Marborn, Eckardroth, and Wahlert, and Kerbersdorf, held by von Hutten, Electoral Mainz, and Salmünster Abbey.

The remaining entries include Roist von Waers at Wackernheim, Wörrstadt, Fürfeld, Sauerschwabenheim, and Berkersheim (1684/1762); J. J. Roth von Rohrbach [identified as J. J. Rode, 1697] and his wife, née Pistorius von Nidda, at Nieder- and Ober-Eschbach, with debts to J. Max and Pauly of Frankfurt and notary J. C. Schnorr of Frankfurt (1703/1705); Schelm von Bergen at Berkersheim, Seckbach, Dorn-Assenheim, and Kaichen (1697/1729); J. H. von Schenk zu Schweinsberg, formerly von Bicken, at Siegen and its district (1629), with G. D. Ebel of Giessen; von Schoenbeck at Düsseldorf (1706); J. W. von [Weitolshausen genannt] Schrautenbach at Giessen, Hahnstätten, and Lohrheim in the Unterlahn district (1633); and the widow M. J. S. Schütz von Holzhausen, née von Lindau, who in 1653 sold to Jakob Rost and his wife A. M., née Riedesel von Bellersheim, her half of the free noble estate at Ober- and Nieder-Florstadt. In 1650 she had exchanged that half for her estate at Hornau with J. D. von Rosenbach; J. H. Schenck von Schweinsberg held the other half. There is also an c. 1700 assessment of the free noble estate at Seckbach (owner unnamed); von Seraing, formerly von Steprode, at Faulbach and Hoffheim near Hadamar (1763, with extracts from 1547 onward); J. G. Siegfried, surgeon at Nieder-Florstadt (1764); von Solemacher at Bleidenbach, Bochel, Herold, Himmighofen, Klingelbach, and Weyer (1735/1746); the Graf von Solms-Hungen at Bellersheim and Birklar (1676/1678); a Graf von Spaur, chamber judge at Wetzlar, at Rockenberg (1788); J. P. Stahl at Ober-Eschbach, formerly Riedesel (c. 1760); Philipp M. von Stein-Kallenfels zu Meisenheim at Härtlingen and Langwiesen in the Oberwesterwald district, formerly von Irmtraut (1794, 1688); division of Steinfurth property (1765); Philipp E. von Stockheim at Geisenheim, Ehrenfels, Roßdorf near Darmstadt, Gau-Bickelheim, Hanau, Ober-Olm, Finthen, and Gonsenheim (1655); J. Fr. H. G. Stockhorner von Starein at Kaichen (1735); former von Stubenrauch property at Rockenberg (1771); Josef Todescho, Hessian saltworks director at Schmalkalden, at Bad Nauheim (1738); Philipp Varnbüler at Hanau (1706); J. H. Wentz von Lahnstein’s exchange of property with C. von Selbach genannt Quadfassel at Neunkirchen in the Saarland and Hirzau (1605); and (Fabricius) von Westerfeld at Kesselstadt (1697). A 1663 inventory lists knightly estates in the Westerwald held by von Metternich, von Irmtraut, von Heddesdorf, von Hunolstein, Wentz, von Vallendar, and von Holdingshausen, at Langwiesen, Hadamar, Heringen, Scheuern, Zinzig, Lohrbach, Niederhammerstein, Heddesdorf, Irmtraut in the Limburg district, Eltz, Kiedrich, Bendorf, Beuel, Lutzingen near Breisig, Waldmannshausen in the Limburg district, Niederlahnstein, and Ehrenbreitstein. Finally, Philipp H. J. W. von Winter is listed as family senior at Friedberg’s Judengasse (1764). The file’s stated term is 1651–1771.
